ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a small ball with mass $m=0.1\mathrm{kg}$ is thrown horizontally from point $O$ at the right end of a horizontal platform with an initial velocity $v_{0}$. After leaving the platform, the ball falls tangentially into a vertical smooth circular track $A B C$ at point $A$ and just passes through the highest point $C$ along the track. The shape of the circular track $A B C$ is a circle with radius $R=2.5\mathrm{m}$ from which a $127^{\circ}$ arc at the upper left corner has been removed. $C B$ is its vertical diameter ($\sin53^{\circ}=0.8$, $\cos53^{\circ}=0.6$, gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and air resistance is negligible). Find:

1. What is the magnitude of the velocity $v_{C}$ of the small ball as it passes through point $C$?
2. What is the magnitude of the supporting force exerted by the track on the small ball when it reaches the lowest point $B$ of the track?
3. What is the vertical height \( H \) from point \( O \) at the end of the platform to point \( A \)?

After leaving the platform, the ball falls tangentially into a vertical smooth circular track $ABC$ at point $A$ and just passes through the highest point $C$ along the track. The shape of the circular track $ABC$ is a circle with radius $R=2.5\mathrm{m}$ from which a $127^{\circ}$ arc at the upper left corner has been removed. $CB$ is its vertical diameter ($\sin53^{\circ}=0.8$, $\cos53^{\circ}=0.6$, gravitational acceleration $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and air resistance is negligible). Find: 1. the magnitude of the velocity $v_C$ of the small ball as it passes through point $C$; 2. the magnitude of the supporting force exerted by the track on the small ball when it reaches the lowest point $B$ of the track; 3. the vertical height $H$ from point $O$ to point $A$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a horizontal platform, point O is located at the right end of the platform, and the small ball is thrown horizontally to the right from O, with an arrow marking the initial velocity v0. The vertical distance from O to the horizontal dashed line passing through point A is marked as H. On the right side is part of a smooth circular track in a vertical plane, CB is the vertical diameter, C is at the highest point, and B is at the lowest point. The center of the circle is on CB, a dashed radius connects to A, and the angle between this radius and the vertical radius pointing downward toward B is 53°; A is located at the lower left of the center of the circle. Reasoning: The small ball just passes through the highest point C, so the track support force at point C is zero, and from the centripetal force condition mg = m v_C^2 / R, we get v_C = sqrt(gR) = sqrt(10 × 2.5) = 5 m/s. From C to B, the vertical drop height is 2R, and by conservation of mechanical energy, v_B^2 = v_C^2 + 2g(2R) = 25 + 2 × 10 × 5 = 125. At point B, along the radius upward toward the center of the circle, the force equation is N - mg = m v_B^2 / R, so N = mg + m v_B^2 / R = 0.1 × 10 + 0.1 × 125 / 2.5 = 1 + 5 = 6.0 N. From the geometric relationship in the figure, point A is lower than the center of the circle by R cos53°, and point C is higher than the center of the circle by R, so the vertical rise height from A to C is R + R cos53° = 2.5 × (1 + 0.6) = 4.0 m. By conservation of mechanical energy from A to C, v_A^2 = v_C^2 + 2g(R + R cos53°) = 25 + 2 × 10 × 4.0 = 105. The small ball enters the track tangentially at point A, and the velocity direction is perpendicular to the radius; since the angle between the radius and the vertical direction in the figure is 53°, the tangential velocity direction is 53° below the horizontal, so the magnitude of the vertical component of v_A is v_A sin53°. The small ball is thrown horizontally from O, and the initial vertical velocity is zero, so (v_A sin53°)^2 = 2gH. Therefore H = v_A^2 sin^2 53° / (2g) = 105 × 0.8^2 / 20 = 3.36 m.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small ball with mass $m=0.1\mathrm{kg}$ is thrown horizontally from point $O$ at the right end of a horizontal platform with an initial velocity $v_0$. After leaving the platform, the ball falls tangentially into a vertical smooth circular track $ABC$ at point $A$ and just passes through the highest point $C$ along the track. The shape of the circular track $ABC$ is a circle with radius $R=2.5\mathrm{m}$ from which a $127^{\circ}$ arc at the upper left corner has been removed. $CB$ is its vertical diameter ($\sin53^{\circ}=0.8$, $\cos53^{\circ}=0.6$, gravitational acceleration $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, and air resistance is negligible). Find: 1. the magnitude of the velocity $v_C$ of the small ball as it passes through point $C$; 2. the magnitude of the supporting force exerted by the track on the small ball when it reaches the lowest point $B$ of the track; 3. the vertical height $H$ from point $O$ to point $A$.
